title: Functions for Extracting NSEC and ECx Values from fitted Frequentist and Bayesian Model Objects
text: Contemporary ecotoxicology increasingly relies model-based inference derive toxicity metrics concentration–response data. However, statistical tools used estimate metrics remain fragmented, inconsistently defined, often tied specific modelling frameworks. inconsistencies hinder transparency, reproducibility, comparability regulatory decision-making. core aim toxval operationalise NSEC estimation across frequentist Bayesian concentration–response models generalise capability broader suite toxicity metrics. , package highlights critical often overlooked issue ecotoxicology: ambiguity definition “effect.” ECx values — widely used — depend effect defined relative controls, model structure, response scale, leading inconsistencies always transparent users (see issue #19). toxval addresses challenges providing: consistent interface extracting ECx, NOEC, NSEC values fitted models; support multiple model classes inference frameworks; explicit, transparent definitions effect -effect independent model class; improved reproducibility comparability toxicity estimates across modelling approaches.

text: -Significant-Effect Concentration (NSEC) model-based alternative traditional -Observed-Effect Concentration (NOEC). Planned improvements include: clearer documentation type argument ("relative", "absolute", "direct") appropriate; explicit warnings ECx definitions poorly defined given model family (e.g., unbounded Gaussian responses); transparent exposure reference points (e.g., top, bottom, control) used calculation.
